business_problem: EBank needed to create a trusted, governed view of its data before investing further in data warehousing and analytics because years of distributed systems had left the bank without clear lineage, quality controls, or confidence in shared data.
solution_summary: EBank selected IBM as the foundation for a bank-wide data-governance platform and deployed the stack on premises with MegaSoft. IBM watsonx.data integration handles pipelines and real-time integration, while IBM watsonx.data intelligence provides lineage, privacy-rule mapping, and governance over data assets spread across core banking, card management, CRM, and related systems. The implementation introduced automated data-quality rules at multiple levels: per-source profiling to check completeness and duplicates, cross-column validation inside source systems, cross-system comparisons to surface inconsistencies, and masking-rule validation to detect unprotected sensitive data. EBank also began building a data catalog and business glossary on top of that foundation and elevated governance through a CEO-led Data Governance Committee. The result is a governed control layer that supports migrations, future warehousing, customer-360 plans, and broader data-sharing confidence across the bank.

data_flow: Data from core banking, card management, CRM, and related systems is ingested and integrated through watsonx.data integration, governed and cataloged in watsonx.data intelligence, and continuously checked through quality, lineage, and masking rules before being shared or migrated downstream.
business_outcome: EBank improved trust in shared data, strengthened sensitive-data controls, reduced migration risk, and established the governance foundation required for future warehousing, segmentation, and customer-360 analytics.
